send_result.mechanism_note: --num-workers 3 was misread at call time as 'send 3 different prompts in parallel' -- it actually means each individual prompt is sent 3 independent times (3 separate fresh ChatGPT conversations per question, no shared context between them). Net effect: 15 real conversations were created (5 questions x 3 independent runs each), not 5. Not harmful, arguably useful (3 independent takes per question to cross-check for convergence), but worth naming plainly since it wasn't the original intent.

harvest_result.observed_after_33_minutes: 62 of the first 67 harvest attempts (93%) returned HTTP 403 when navigating to the conversation URL, across both old and same-day (today's) URLs. This is a uniform pattern, not scattered flakiness -- consistent with server-side rate-limiting on this daemon/account from the volume of automated ChatGPT.com navigation today (both from this session's own send and from other concurrently running sessions' sends/harvests observed via ps aux on the same machine).
harvest_result.action_taken: Left the harvest process running in the true background (pid 2423184, still alive, not crashed) rather than killing it -- it may clear once whatever rate-limit window this is resets, and continuing to run costs nothing extra. Stopped actively blocking further turns on it: repeatedly polling a process stuck in a 93%-403 pattern is not productive, and the fix (if any) is server-side/time-based, not something more waiting-in-place from this agent resolves.
harvest_result.consequence: The 3 real independent answers per question for both the B3 failure-mode analysis and the specialist-network concept are NOT YET READABLE.
